title: Work IQ: granular MCP policies to restrict platforms, workloads and operations
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the current Microsoft documentation. It distinguishes the planned granular policies from the existing tenant policy switch, reports the differing write-operation defaults in the two cited experiences, and correctly identifies consumption billing through Copilot Credits.

claims.quote: Provide granular policies that restrict MCP access to trusted platforms, workloads, and supported operations.

claims.claim: Work IQ has a Rego-based policy layer.

claims.claim: The policy layer evaluates each MCP tool request at request time.
claims.quote: Policy layer | Applies tenant governance rules to each MCP tool request

claims.claim: The policy layer can allow or deny MCP tool requests.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control applies across the tenant.
claims.quote: When you turn on the policy, it applies across the tenant and helps control MCP tool access at request time.

claims.claim: The documented initial policy control is a tenant-wide on/off switch in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: The policy page says more granular controls and templates might be added later.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API or cmdlet for the tenant Work IQ MCP policy at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy settings Microsoft Graph beta API update policy Allowed Disallowed PowerShell; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Work IQ" "policy". Read Policy governance for Work IQ MCP and returned results; no policy-setting call is documented.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy platform workload per-agent operation restrictions admin API. Read Policy governance for Work IQ MCP and Work IQ in Copilot Studio; neither documents the planned granular policy UI or API. Maker workload scoping is a different control.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API uses consumption-based licensing through Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ granular MCP policies licensing price Copilot Credits separate charge. Read Work IQ API overview, Work IQ overview, Policy governance for Work IQ MCP and licensing search results; no separate granular-policy charge is stated.

claims.claim: Work IQ costs can be managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage and can be managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users get Work IQ in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.

claims.claim: The policy configuration instructions require an account permitted to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings.
claims.quote: Sign in with an account that has permission to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings.

claims.claim: The Learn policy instructions name no specific administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "role". Read Policy governance for Work IQ MCP in full and the returned excerpts; its instructions specify permission to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings, not a named administrator role.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises checking tenant access to Work IQ MCP if the policy settings do not appear.
claims.quote: If you don't see the Work IQ MCP policy settings, check that your tenant has access to Work IQ MCP and that your admin account has the required permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises checking the administrator account's permissions if policy settings do not appear.
claims.quote: If you don't see the Work IQ MCP policy settings, check that your tenant has access to Work IQ MCP and that your admin account has the required permissions.

claims.claim: The Work IQ service principal is automatically created on first use of Work IQ.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Configuring MCP policy before any MCP use can fail because the service principal has not been provisioned.
claims.quote: In some corner cases, such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs tenant administrators to Enable your tenant for Work IQ to provision the missing service principal.
claims.quote: Tenant administrators can provision it by following the steps in Enable your tenant for Work IQ.

claims.claim: The policy page refers to experiences configuring policy settings and to editable policies.
claims.quote: If your experience configures policy settings, update only editable policies and validate values before sending updates.

claims.claim: The policy page describes toggle values such as Allowed and Disallowed.
claims.quote: Toggle-style settings use values such as Allowed and Disallowed.

claims.claim: The policy governance page names no policy configuration endpoint or cmdlet.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "API" "settings"; Work IQ MCP policy settings Microsoft Graph beta API update policy Allowed Disallowed PowerShell. Read Policy governance for Work IQ MCP in full; it gives UI steps and policy concepts but no configuration endpoint or cmdlet.

claims.claim: The migration guide describes tenant-wide blocking of Work IQ MCP as stopping it for the whole tenant.
claims.quote: Block Work IQ MCP tenant-wide only when you intend to stop it for the entire tenant.

claims.claim: The migration guide does not give the navigation path for tenant-wide MCP blocking.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "API" "settings". Read Migrate agentic retrieval workflows to Work IQ MCP in full; it mentions tenant-wide blocking and links policy governance but provides no blocking UI path.

claims.claim: Policy approval does not guarantee success because access is still checked against the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: Policy approval doesn't guarantee the operation succeeds. If policy allows an MCP tool request, the underlying resource access is still checked against the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions.
